question.value: How do the molecular (ALMA CO(3-2)) and ionised ([OIII], GTC/MEGARA) outflow phases of the Seyfert galaxy NGC 5506 compare, and how do they couple to the disc?

evidence.quote: In this study, we investigate the molecular and ionised gas phases of NGC 5506, an Sa spiral galaxy in the GATOS sample
(project-ID: #2017.1.00082.S; PI: S. García-Burillo)
We observed NGC 5506 with the Band 7 ALMA receiver and a single pointing
ALMA Band 7 observations of the CO($3-2$) transition

method.value: 3DBarolo ring fits, first with vrad=0 then with free vrad

evidence.quote: We modelled the CO($3-2$) datacube with ^3D^BAROLO[^2] (cite: diteodoro15), which creates a disc model for the rotating gas by dividing the emission into concentric rings

key_parameters.value: 0.15" (~19 pc) rings, 60 rings, centre fixed at continuum peak

evidence.quote: We set a ring radial size of $0.15 \ensuremath{''}$ ($\simeq 19$ pc), similar to the ALMA beam ($0.21 \ensuremath{''} \times 0.13 \ensuremath{''}$), and a total of 60 rings

assumptions.value: Outflow velocities are upper limits because bar elliptical motions possible

evidence.loc: 4.2 Rotating disc with a radial velocity component
evidence.quote: we conservatively assume that the outflow velocities we derive between $R_{out,min}^{\rm mol} = 0.4 \ensuremath{''}$ (50 pc) and $R_{out,max}^{\rm mol} = 5 \ensuremath{''}$ (610 pc) are upper limits

validation.value: Compared PV diagrams and mean velocities along minor axis for models with and without vrad; vsys compared with literature

evidence.loc: 4.2 Rotating disc with a radial velocity component
evidence.quote: Fig. [6](#fig:barolo_PV) shows the PV diagrams of this run, where we can appreciate a better fit along the minor axis

evidence.quote: Assuming a simple shell geometry (cite: alonsoherrero23), we can write the mass outflow rate as

evidence.quote: a Galactic CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $X_{\rm CO} = 2 \times 10^{20}$ mol cm$^{-2}$ (K km s$^{-1}$)$^{-1}$

method.value: Spaxel-by-spaxel ALUCINE fit with 1 or 2 Gaussians, AoN>3; broad = outflow, narrow = rotation

evidence.quote: The ALUCINE code determines, based on the AoN $>3$ cut, whether one or two Gaussians are necessary for each spaxel.
we achieved better results by setting $v_{sys, \text{[OIII]}}=1893$ km s$^{-1}$
See Fig. [21](#fig:residuals).

method.value: Percentile velocities (v02..v98, W80, Δv) from sum of two Gaussians per spaxel

evidence.quote: For every spaxel we calculate the velocities corresponding to different percentiles to the flux contained in the modelled line profile

method.value: logU from Baron & Netzer 2019 line-ratio relation -> n_e; extinction-corrected broad [OIII] luminosity; M = mu m_H L/(gamma n_e); Mdot = M v/R

evidence.quote: Finally, the ionised outflow mass $M_{\rm out}^{\rm ion}$ is given by (cite: rose18; baron19):

key_parameters.value: Cardelli extinction law, R_V=3.1; intrinsic Ha/Hb=3.1; mu=1.4; central pixel r = half pixel size

evidence.quote: we assume an intrinsic ratio $H \alpha / H \beta = 3.1$, and we use the (cite: cardelli89) extinction law ($R_V = 3.1$)

assumptions.value: Broad component is outflow; n_H ~ n_e

evidence.quote: we consider the flux of the broad component as the outflow (whereas the narrow component is associated to the ordered gas rotation)

validation.value: Compared logU, n_e, L[OIII] with Davies et al. 2020 X-shooter values

evidence.quote: We recover a median value of $\log U = -2.9$, in agreement with the integrated value of $-2.87 \pm 0.12$ found by (cite: davies20)

method.value: Energy and momentum rates (E=Mdot v^2/2, P=Mdot v); overlay of Mdot_ion on CO dispersion; compare with radio/X-ray literature

evidence.quote: These two quantities can be straightforwardly calculated as $\dot{E}_{\rm out} = \dot{M}_{\rm out} v_{\rm out}^2 / 2$ and $\dot{P}_{\rm out} = \dot{M}_{\rm out} v_{\rm out}$.

evidence.loc: 4.2 Rotating disc with a radial velocity component
evidence.quote: We find $v_{\rm rot}$ reaching $193$ km s$^{-1}$ at $r = 3.5 \ensuremath{''}$ (440 pc)
We calculate $M_{\rm out}^{\rm mol} = 1.75 \times 10^8$ M$_{\odot}$
we find $v_{\rm out}^{\rm mol} = 25.6 \pm 9.4$ km s$^{-1}$
$\dot{M}_{\rm out}^{\rm mol} = 8 \pm 3$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$
up to $\dot{M}_{out,max}^{\rm mol} = 28$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$
We recover a median value of $\log U = -2.9$
The maximum $n_{e, \text{max}} = 8.5 \times 10^5$ cm$^{-3}$ is exactly at the AGN position.
We calculated a total ionised outflowing mass of $M_{\rm out}^{\rm ion} = 9.8 \times 10^4$ M$_{\odot}$.
we find $v_{\rm out}^{\rm ion} = 422 \pm 97$ km s$^{-1}$
The maximum value observed is $W_{80, max} = 826$ km s$^{-1}$ located $\sim 6 \ensuremath{''}$ W.
which in our case is $\dot{P}_{\rm mol} / \dot{P}_{\rm ion} = 7$

findings_qualitative.value: BPT diagrams show AGN-dominated excitation in both narrow and broad components

evidence.quote: we can conclude that most of the observed central emission is due to the AGN activity rather than star formation, both for the narrow and broad components.

findings_qualitative.value: Ionised gas rotates slower than molecular gas (~60%)

evidence.quote: Interestingly, the ionised gas seems to be rotating at $60 \%$ the velocity of the molecular gas.

claims.hypothesis: Does the molecular disc of NGC 5506 host an outflow?
claims.experiment: 3DBarolo model of CO(3-2) with radial velocity component
claims.result: Mean outward vrad 25.6±9.4 km/s, Mdot_mol = 8±3 Msun/yr (upper limit)
claims.finding: Rotating and outflowing molecular ring, with possible inflow inside 0.4"

evidence.quote: interpreted as a rotating and outflowing molecular ring.

claims.hypothesis: What is the ionised outflow rate?
claims.experiment: Two-Gaussian decomposition, percentile velocities, logU density method
claims.result: Mdot_ion = 0.076±0.017 Msun/yr, v=422±97 km/s within 525 pc
claims.finding: Ionised outflow is much weaker in mass rate than molecular

evidence.quote: resulting in an ionised mass outflow rate of $\dot{M}_{\rm out}^{\rm ion} = 0.076 \pm 0.017$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$.

claims.experiment: Overlay of Mdot_ion map and CO dispersion
claims.result: Spatial correlation with high CO dispersion
claims.finding: Weak coupling, ionised bicone partially intercepts the disc; multiple outflow episodes

evidence.quote: We compared the spatially resolved map of $\dot{M}_{\rm out}^{\rm ion}$ with the CO($3-2$) velocity dispersion map, identifying spatial correlation between the two.

why_this_method.value: Galactic X_CO chosen for comparison with literature and no merger/IR luminosity

evidence.quote: We chose the Galactic value to better compare our results with most of the literature
we limited our analysis to two components to have a simpler interpretation of them

limitations_admitted.value: Inflow within 0.4" not confirmable (only two radial points)

referee_caveats_inferred: 3DBarolo radial velocity in a highly inclined (80 deg) disc is degenerate with non-circular motion
Mdot assumes shell geometry and average velocity; r31 and X_CO uncertain
No uncertainties propagated from fits; scatter used as error
Ionised outflow area limited by Hbeta broad component
